quote_text:
How difficult to watch was that for you? I think, like, um, first of all,  
congratulations to Kilmarnock on their victory  and already, um, to our fans traveling here  
the day after Christmas. I think, in focus  on our performance today, it is not, uh,  
acceptable how we performed today. Like, uh, how  we compete with Kilmarnock was not good enough.
First of all, I have to say Kilmarnock  is doing their thing really well. They're  
good in what they're doing. They're good in how  they win the second balls, how they put crosses,  
how they arrive, how they defend. But we have  to compete much, much more when we are playing.
Um, hopefully, this was the worst  performance of the season, and,  
uh, that—you can win games, you can draw  games, you can lose games—but not the way  
we did today. This effort we make for each  other out there today is not good enough.
Do you talk about confidence?  Does that play a part as well? 
I think, like, uh, you can get  in, uh, some part of the season,  
sometimes get in a really  bad run. Uh, I think, uh,  
we haven’t won for some games now. But some  games—Hearts, Hibs away—at least we compete.
Today, they win every duel. They win  every second ball. They win everything,  
every duel on the pitch, and then it's not easy  to win football games. Um, and if you’re also  
adding how we play with the ball today, because  I’m a part of this—I’m the coach, and my staff  
and the players—we have to look ourselves in the  mirror and do much, much better the next game.
It’s not long until the next game; it’s on Sunday,  
away against Dundee United. But we have  to perform much better than we did today.
Do you have to bear your teeth at times? Because  you've shown the nice side, but your team's not  
applying itself the way you want. Do you feel  you have to show a different side to yourself? 
We have—I talk with my players inside the  dressing room. But, uh, right now, we just need  
to stick together and come back on the pitch with  a much, much better effort than we have done now.
No one can hide. Uh, we have to keep the  head high and go out again and compete.  
There’s no other way. No one else is  going to do it for us. It’s us—me,  
the staff, the players—there’s no  one else going to play the game.
So we have to stick together and  
with much, much more energy and belief. I don’t  like the word confidence. You can’t play good  
one day and then blame confidence. We have to do  our basic things much better than we did today.
We don’t—again, this is the second game  in a row now—how we cover each other when  
we lose the first duel, who picks up  the second ball. These kind of things  
just need to stop. And we have to go out, and  everybody has to do it. That’s the only way.
Does this dip in form undermine what you said  at the start of the season, that patience was  
required and it’s a three-year project? We have a project—what we want to do and  
how we want to look in the future. But right now,  it’s the short term. Like, how can we stop this?
I don’t like to think, “Okay, we are still in  that position in the table, blah blah blah.”  
It’s right now—how we perform right now. And we  have to do much better than we’re doing right now.
We can’t hide behind “we had a good start”  or whatever. Football is not the past,  
it’s not the future. It’s right now. And right  now, we’re not performing well, and we need to  
find a way to stop this, get together, and  do much better. And it starts on Sunday.
Do you sense from your players  they are also frustrated  
after starting the season so successfully? That’s a part of being a football team. Like,  
um, you can be frustrated if you’re performing  well, you do everything—the effort really  
well—and then you lose sometimes.  Okay, congratulations to the opponent.
But the way we performed today, the effort we  made today, is another thing. And that’s why  
we have to just, like—we can’t show this side of  ourselves one more time. That’s not good enough.
title: Jimmy Thelin Post Match Press Conference | Kilmarnock 4-0 Aberdeen
